causes.label: demand
causes.quote: High demand, which peaked at 8,477 MW- the highest up to that point this summer.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Nearly 3,000 MW of baseload capacity was unavailable on the evening of the 9 December. This included about 1,400 MW of outages, while a further 1,600 MW was unavailable due to generators offering less than their registered capacity.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Milmerran unit 1 removed 115 MW of capacity from 5.35 am. 30 MW was removed within 4 hours pre-dispatch.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: A system normal constraint limited access to cheap imports from NSW to around 160 MW. The nominal capacity of QNI is 300 to 600 MW.

constraints_named.quote: A system normal constraint limited access to cheap imports from NSW at the time of the high price event in Queensland.

interconnectors_named.name: Queensland-New South Wales Interconnector (QNI)
interconnectors_named.quote: A system normal constraint limited imports from NSW on the Queensland-New South Wales Interconnector (QNI), further limiting Queensland's access to low-priced generation.

intervals.quote: On 9 December 2021 the wholesale price of electricity in Queensland reached $7,118/MWh and $11,538/MWh for the 6.30 and 7 pm 30-minute periods, respectively.

network_outages.quote: System normal constraints reflect network limits when there are no outages.

peak_price.quote: On 9 December 2021 the wholesale price of electricity in Queensland reached $7,118/MWh and $11,538/MWh for the 6.30 and 7 pm 30-minute periods, respectively.

rebid_set_price.quote: Rebidding of capacity from low to high prices did not contribute to prices above $5,000/MWh.
